one_liner: JVM event-loop HTTP toolkit on Netty; beats some C++ servers on HttpArena but trails nginx, h2o and mongoose on scored profiles.
what_it_does: Vert.x core is a Java toolkit for non-blocking network applications: HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, TCP, TLS, timers and file I/O on Netty event loops, with handlers registered as callbacks or Futures. vertx-web adds a Router with path and query parameters, body handling and JSON helpers. It is a library you embed in a JVM application (deployed as one 'verticle' instance per core), not a drop-in replacement for a C web server's configuration.
how_it_is_fast: Each verticle instance is pinned to one Netty event loop and all instances share the listening port, so request handling is lock-free per connection and needs no thread per request; long waits (the /delay test) are event-loop timers, so 32,000 pending requests cost memory rather than threads. HTTP/1.1 parsing and encoding come from Netty's codec (netty-codec-http). The HotSpot JIT compiles the hot path after warm-up; the HttpArena entry also returns minimal 66-byte responses (status line, content-type, content-length, body, no Date or Server header; derived from 741.43 MiB/s divided by 11,782,768 req/s), which helps most on the pipelined test.
when_to_use: JVM services that must hold tens of thousands of mostly idle or slow connections (long polls, delayed responses): HttpArena async-32000 shows 1.86M req/s against Drogon 143K and userver 409K.
Pipelined or high-request-rate HTTP/1.1 APIs on a many-core box where a Java stack is required and C/C++ is not an option.
Teams that want Netty-level throughput with routing, JSON and TLS already wired, instead of hand-writing Netty channel pipelines.
Gzip JSON APIs, where the json-comp-4096 row (256,544 req/s) is level with hical (0.98x) and proxygen (1.05x), behind userver (0.86x) and twice Drogon's.
when_not_to_use: As a replacement for nginx, h2o or mongoose on plain HTTP/1.1, TLS or static files: 0.46x to 0.61x of them on baseline-4096 and json-tls-4096 and 0.27x of nginx on static-tls-1024.

Short-lived connections: limited-conn-4096 (reconnect every 10 requests) reaches 602,586 req/s vs 2.4M to 2.7M for nginx, h2o, mongoose, hical and libreactorng, while using only 3,255% CPU of the 64 threads (the others use 5,448% to 6,644%), which points to connection setup rather than request handling as the limit (inferred).

Memory- or CPU-constrained hosts: 2.4 GiB resident when nearly idle (latency-10k) vs 50 to 73 MiB for hical, mongoose, libreactorng and Drogon; 30.3 us CPU per request at a paced 1M req/s vs 21.0 to 22.5 us for libreactorng, mongoose and hical (Drogon 32.1 us); on 8 logical CPUs it held only 75% of a 500K req/s target (2.48 s average latency) where libreactorng held 99.8%.
Workloads that cannot tolerate JIT warm-up or GC pauses: HttpArena reports the best of three 5 s runs, so cold-start cost is not in the numbers.

HTTP/2-heavy services expecting the 5.0 fast path: open bug #6143 reports a 5-8% h2c regression in 5.1.0, and the maintainer plans to move HTTP/1.1 onto the same generic path, accepting possibly worse raw performance.

integration.dependencies: Netty (common, buffer, transport, handler, codec-http/http2/http3, resolver) and jackson-core; jackson-databind and the native transports (epoll, io_uring, kqueue) are optional and must be added explicitly
integration.min_toolchain: Java 11 for Vert.x 5 (build toolchains JDK 11 and 21); the HttpArena entry uses JDK 21 (eclipse-temurin:21)
integration.platforms: any JVM platform; native epoll and io_uring on Linux, kqueue on BSD/macOS, JDK NIO elsewhere (the HttpArena entry ships no native transport jar, so it ran on NIO; inferred from its pom.xml)
integration.thread_safety: Each verticle's handlers run on its own event loop thread and must not block; a blocking call stalls every connection on that loop

gotchas: HttpArena's pipelined win partly reflects response size: its /pipeline check only requires the body 'ok' and Content-Type text/plain, and the Vert.x entry sends 66-byte responses with no Date or Server header against about 142 bytes for nginx (derived from bandwidth divided by req/s); the profile is reference-only and libreactorng (C) is 3.7x faster there anyway.

Memory numbers are partly configuration: the Dockerfile runs G1 with -XX:+AlwaysPreTouch and no -Xms or -Xmx, so the resident size reflects pre-touched default-sized heap as much as working set (inferred); the reported 4.8 to 16.9 GiB rows should not be read as a minimum.

The measured release is 5.1.6; 5.1.10 and 5.2.1 were tagged on 2026-10-07, so current releases may differ, and the latency-500k-8cpu row (rate_ratio 0.75) is one the harness itself flags as not comparable on CPU because the offered rate was not held.

Cross-run comparison: the Vert.x, nginx and mongoose result files were written on different dates (2026-09-06, 2026-08-30, 2026-09-21 per the verifier), so small gaps (for example json-comp vs hical, 0.98x) are within run-to-run noise.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Vert.x over raw Netty when you want routing, JSON and TLS without writing channel handlers, and over Quarkus (which runs on Vert.x) when you want the toolkit without a full framework on top; on the same HttpArena suite actix-web (2.78M), the tokio entry (4.19M) and every C entry post higher baseline-4096 numbers than its 1.99M, so choose Vert.x for the JVM ecosystem, not for raw speed.
verified_claims_summary: HttpArena (Vert.x 5.1.6 with vertx-web on JDK 21 G1 vs nginx 1.31.4 -O3 -march=native with a custom C handler, plus h2o, mongoose, libreactorng and C++ entries; Threadripper PRO 3995WX, server on 32 cores / 64 threads, best of 3 x 5 s runs) shows Vert.x ahead of C only on the reference-only pipelined-4096 row (11.78M vs nginx 4.04M req/s, but 0.27x libreactorng) and ahead of most C++ entries on async-32000 (1.86M vs Drogon 0.14M), while it runs at 0.23x to 0.61x of nginx on the scored baseline, limited-conn, json-tls and static-tls rows.
status_note: Very active (tags 5.2.1, 5.1.10 and 4.5.35 on 2026-10-07, 14.7k stars), dual EPL-2.0/Apache-2.0, and a mature production toolkit; its catalogue value is as a fast JVM option, not as a C/C++ replacement.
